name: Heat-related deaths
definition: Deaths of New York City residents caused directly by heat (heat stroke and other heat illness coded X30 or T67 on the death certificate), May through September, by year.

source.name: NYC Department of Health and Mental Hygiene, 2026 NYC Heat-Related Mortality Report (Figure 1) and 2021 report (heat-stress death table)

method: Annual counts of heat-stress deaths among NYC residents, May-September. 2016-2025 are the Figure 1 values of the 2026 Heat-Related Mortality Report (read from the chart's published data file); 2010-2015 are from the table in the 2021 report (https://a816-dohbesp.nyc.gov/IndicatorPublic/data-features/heat-report-archive/2021/). Overlapping years 2016, 2017, 2018 match in both reports.
caveats: This is the heat-stress (directly caused) count, not the larger heat-exacerbated estimate. The report's estimate of heat-exacerbated (excess) deaths, about 490 a year on average for 2014-2023, is published only as a multi-year average from a statistical model, not as annual counts, so it cannot be used as the annual series.
Counts are small and swing with single heat waves: the 2026 report counts 21 heat-stress deaths in 2025, 19 of them from the June 22-25 heat wave.
The 2026 report says the most recent year's count is provisional because mortality records are not yet final.
